info.title: Infini Analytics
info.description:
Track and monitor the complete lifecycle of your automations with Infini Analytics.

Send start events (START), intermediate milestones (EVENT), non-critical warnings (WARNING), errors (ERROR) and completion events (END) to get full traceability and audit trails for every execution in your organization.

**Getting started:**

1. Get your **organization token** from the Infini platform (Settings → Organization).

2. Find your **automation ID** (`automation_id`) in the automations list.

3. Define a unique **execution ID** (`execution_id`) — it can be an internal system ID or a timestamp.

4. Record events throughout the execution using the *Register event* action.

An execution is considered **successful** if it ends with END without any prior ERROR. As soon as an ERROR is recorded, the execution is marked as **failed**.

post.description:
Records an event in the lifecycle of an automation. Use this action at each key point of your flow to get complete traceability.

**Recommended event flow:**

- **START** → at the beginning of the flow, before any business logic.

- **EVENT** → at important milestones (data reading, processing, sending...).

- **WARNING** → if something is not ideal but the flow can continue.

- **ERROR** → if an exception or failure occurs. Marks the execution as failed.

- **END** → upon successful completion. Marks the execution as successful.

**Note:** The `error_id` and `error_description` fields only apply when the event type is ERROR.

automation_id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the automation in the Infini platform. Find it in the automations list or ask your administrator. Format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.

execution_id.description: Unique identifier for this specific execution. Must be unique across simultaneous executions of the same automation. Use the same value for all events within the same execution. Can be an internal system ID or a timestamp (e.g. "2025-03-03T15:32:17").

event.description: Event type to record in this call. START: start of execution. EVENT: relevant intermediate milestone. WARNING: non-critical warning (flow continues). ERROR: failure or exception (marks execution as failed). END: successful end of execution.

description.description: Free text describing the event. It will appear in the execution history on the Infini platform. Being descriptive is recommended to facilitate subsequent auditing.

error_id.description: Only for ERROR event type. Error identifier code. Can be a code defined by your team (e.g. "e0001") or one automatically provided by the automation platform.

error_description.description: Only for ERROR event type. Full error message, including the stacktrace or exception message provided by your automation platform (Power Automate, Python, etc.).
error_description.example: NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.

automation.description: UUID of the automation where the event was recorded

execution_id.description: Execution identifier, as sent in the request

type_of_event.description: Type of event that was recorded (START, EVENT, WARNING, END or ERROR)

error_id.description: Recorded error code (only applies for ERROR events)

error_description_detail.description: Detailed error description (only applies for ERROR events)

created_at.description: UTC date and time when the event was recorded in the Infini system

401.description: Invalid or missing authentication token. Verify that the "token" header contains the correct value obtained from the Infini platform.

500.description: Internal server error. This may indicate an unusually high load or a temporary issue. If it persists, contact analytics@infini.es.

error.description: Description of the error that occurred

api_key.name: token
api_key.description: Organization token obtained from the Infini platform. Find it under Settings → Organization → Token. Without this token or with an invalid token you will receive an HTTP 401 error.

x-ms-openai-manifest.modelDescription: Connector to record and monitor the complete lifecycle of automations using Infini Analytics. Allows sending START (execution start), EVENT (intermediate milestone), WARNING (non-critical notice), ERROR (failure, marks execution as failed) and END (successful completion) events, associated with a specific automation and execution. Requires an organization token from the Infini platform.
